summary: Pennsylvania steel Aermotor tower on Tuscarora Mountain, built 1921 and removed 1978; no source describes what remains at the summit.

facts.status_note: Removed in 1978; no source describes what remains at the summit today.
facts.agency: Pennsylvania Department of Forestry (built 1921); the land is now Buchanan State Forest

events.note: Built by the state in 1921; a September 1921 report said it was finished, about 80 feet from the ground.
The register entry for Big Knob says its 1914 tree tower was replaced by Tuscarora in 1921.
Registered September 16, 2008; nominated by Henry Isenberg.

evidence.quote: This steel Aermotor tower was built in 1921 and was removed in 1978.
Orders for 50 towers have been placed with the manufacturers.

evidence.quote: Two of the fifty steel fire towers that will be erected by the Pennsylvania Department of Forestry this summer probably will be placed in the Buchanan State Forest

evidence.supports: August 1921: one of first 18 towers at Tuscarora, Franklin county
evidence.quote: One of the first 18 towers will be put up at Tuscarora, Franklin county.

evidence.supports: 2,540 feet above sea level, about 80 feet from the ground, on the mountain top
evidence.quote: stands on the top of Tuscarora mountain 2540 feet above sea level, a real lookout tower eighty feet from the ground.
at an elevation of 2,440 feet above sea level

evidence.supports: Tower Road vista at about 2,458 feet on Tuscarora Mountain in Buchanan State Forest
evidence.quote: At about 2,458 feet, the Tower Road site on Tuscarora Mountain in Buchanan State Forest provides a magnificent vista

corrections.why: The August 1921 notice names Franklin county, and the 2016 DCNR publication places the Tower Road site in Franklin County. firetower.org says Fulton, so confirm before changing.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: firetower.org lists Fulton County; the 1921 notice and the 2016 DCNR publication say Franklin. The story reports the disagreement and does not settle it.
The June 1921 item gives 2,440 feet and the September 1921 item gives 2,540 feet. The story reports both and does not choose one.

notes_for_editor: No staffing or fire history appears in any source read. Brief coordinates 39.91, -77.95 are about 5 km from the DCNR Tower Road point (39.95030, -77.93648). That point is a vista, not a confirmed tower footprint, so the record's coordinates were left unchanged. Access is left out: DCNR describes a state forest vista but does not connect it to the lookout. The 24.4 m height rests on 'eighty feet from the ground' in a 1921 newspaper item, so it may describe cab height rather than full structure height.
